summary: A granite tower of 1872 on a tide-washed Maine ledge at the mouth of the Piscataqua, built to replace a first tower that stood four decades while storms shook it.

notes_for_editor: Much of the human detail rests on D'Entremont (modern, secondary; he quotes newspapers I could not read: Boston Globe 1911, Portsmouth Herald, Portsmouth Journal 1828). Lighthouse Board reports pre-1891 are not in the corpus, so the 1830 tower, 1870 appropriation and 1871 progress are not checked against primary reports. Whaleback appears in the Board's reports as 'New Hampshire'; the 1912 Bulletin lists it as Me. The record's 15 m tower height is not confirmed (sources give 50 ft/75 ft). Sources disagree on pier and tower size (LF 48/22/32 ft vs D'Entremont 42/32/38 ft), cost, keeper Wetzel's start (1897 vs 1899) and White's end (1941 vs 1942). Keeper roster matched from USLHS lines; relationships among Barr/Amee people not stated in any source. Chronicling America searches returned only whaleback steamers (noise). Family relationship of the 2 Barrs and Mary Amee left unstated in prose. Fact-check 2026-10-27: the 832-hour fog-signal figure is from the fiscal 1891 report (the volume's first report), not 1892; corrected. Roster lines matched by archive heading, not OCR table.
